synopsis: CRJ200 Captain reported a near miss with a UAS while on descent to a Class B airport and reported to ATC.

When a galley oven started to smoke and caught fire on taxi out the Flight Attendant alerted the flight crew and shut off the oven. The fire and smoke dissipated but they returned to the blocks with a CFR escort where; after persuasion; Maintenance removed and replaced/repaired the oven after discovering an electrical heater coil which had burned.
Air carrier Pilot reported being advised by ATC while on approach to MSY that four drones had been sighted below 1000 feet in the final approach corridor to Runway 11.
Air carrier flight crew reported being high on the approach due to task saturation; communications errors and focusing outside for traffic.
A B737-500 flight crew was unable to comply with an ATC directed crossing restriction. The restriction was noted as an 'expect to cross at...' fix on the arrival plate.

A pilot reported that he taxied beyond the DET Runway 33 hold short line on the ramp south of Runway 25 because; looking at the airport taxi diagram; he expected the ramp area to look different and in his confusion missed the faded hold lines on west side of the massive ramp.

A B737 crew reported while descending through 10;000 feet to ANC Runway 7R; ATC changed their Runway to 33. Confused; the crew began setting up for Runway 33 when ATC cleared them for a Runway 7R visual approach; [and to] track the localizer which they discovered out of service. By then seriously distracted; the crew descended below their assigned altitude.
Air carrier Captain reported an uneventful airborne conflict with a Drone (UAV) during approach.
Tower Controller reported observing an aircraft on short final with its landing gear not lowered and issued a go around but the aircraft landed gear up anyway and slid off the runway.
C177 pilot reported a NMAC with a turboprop aircraft in the vicinity of THA airport.

Two helicopters; a MD500 and an AS350; had a near-miss in Class D Airspace after the Tower Controller initially pointed out mutual traffic but provided no updates and the MD500 TCAS did not display traffic.
An instructor pilot described a failure in the nose landing gear retraction/extension system of a Cessna 310 that resulted in landing with a partially extended nose gear.

A corporate jet flight crew reported that after being cleared to cross an active runway they noticed another aircraft commencing takeoff on the same runway. The flight crew stopped prior to crossing the runway; avoiding a potential critical conflict.
Air carrier Captain reported a drone encounter during approach that did not require evasive action.
Air Carrier Captain reported an altitude deviation during arrival.  Captain cited the First Officer's lack of flying and being distracted by a PA as contributing factors.
Flight crew reported that while taxiing across a runway they had a near collision with another aircraft that was taking off from that runway.
During climb a B757 forward galley oven over heated and caught fire. Food from a previous flight caused the fire which subsequently damaged the oven and required a Halon fire extinguisher to contain.
B737NG Captain reported a track deviation occurred when the crew let themselves get rushed in executing a clearance change.
An Instructor pilot reported they detected conflicting traffic on their ADSB and had to take evasive action to avoid a collision. They received no traffic information from ATC.
Air carrier Captain reported flying over an opposite direction UAV while on final approach.
An Air Carrier pilot reported an incorrect crossing restriction for a STAR in the FMC Database.

A Cessna CJ3-25B crew mistook ATC's revised heading clearance; given during takeoff; for an altitude change and climbed on a heading not intended or expected by ATC; creating a conflict with another aircraft. The reporter states several missed opportunities for ATC to notice the misunderstandings during the flight crew's read-back of the clearance instructions and particulars.
Flight crew reported a runway and taxiway incursion while taxiing to the runway at IAG airport. The crew cited signage issues contributed to the event.

Upon receipt of a right main gear unsafe light when they extended the landing gear the flight crew of a DHC-8 declared an emergency; unsuccessfully performed the emergency gear extension checklist; prepared the cabin for an emergency evacuation and ultimately landed safely with the right main still indicating unsafe. Gear pins were inserted by Maintenance and the passengers were deplaned and bussed to the terminal.
Air carrier flight crew reported their aircraft descended below an RNAV Arrival crossing restriction when a runway change was entered in the FMC.
Captain reported encountering a drone while on approach to ATL.
Air carrier Captain and Dispatcher reported aircraft had a landing gear problem but had a safe landing.
PA-28 Pilot reported being distracted and taxiing the aircraft over the runway hold short lines.
Pilot reported a runway incursion partially due to incorrect DXR airport taxiway diagram.
Airbus Captain reported a near miss with a UAV while on final approach to SAN.
Air carrier Captain reported a near miss with a UAS while on a visual approach to a Class B airport. Flight crew notified ATC.
C172 pilot reported a NMAC with another light aircraft in vicinity of FIM VOR.

A CRJ-145 crew reported an odor and haze which developed into heavy smoke after takeoff so an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport. An engine oil seal leak was suspected.
SDF Tower Controller reported they issued a runway crossing clearance to the wrong aircraft due to confusion caused by similar sounding call signs.
Air carrier flight crew reported an altitude deviation due to failed crew communication and the Captain's recent extended time off.
A pilot taxiing for departure reported observing an aircraft taxi onto the active runway without a clearance as another aircraft was on landing roll.
B777 flight crew reported that during cruise flight an oven in the aft galley was on fire.

CE-525 Captain experiences a landing gear failure to extend during approach. A go-around is initiated and the landing gear is blown down successfully but low brake pressure is indicated. The appropriate checklist is complied with and a safe landing ensues.
The pilot of a multi-engine aircraft became aware of another aircraft in close proximity; and took evasive action. ATC was unaware of any traffic in the area; and was unable to identify any on radar.

BE1900 Captain reports failure of the landing gear to extend during approach and notes the landing gear control circuit breaker is tripped. Checklists are consulted and eventually the manual gear extension checklist is employed successfully and an uneventful landing ensues.
UAV flight crew reported that their misunderstanding of a clearance resulted in an altitude deviation.

BE1900 Captain describes an unsafe gear indication during approach resulting in a go around. Manual pumping results in a safe gear indication and a normal landing ensues. The aircraft had a history of unsafe gear indications.
The pilot of a Mooney M20 landed with the gear up but does not recall hearing the gear warning horn. The aircraft was not substantial damaged.
A Pilot reported they may have misunderstood their revised clearance and departed from the wrong runway.
Light Jet Air taxi First Officer reported a near miss with a UAV at 7;000 ft while flying a straight in visual approach to SBY Runway 14. TRACON Controller showed no interest in the event.

Air carrier flight crew was questioned by Approach Control when they had failed to program an 'expect to cross at' note on the WAVUN into their FMS while on descent into FLL and; as a result; failed to meet the restriction when it was given.

An air carrier Captain reported the failure of the autoflight system to comply with the altitude and speed restrictions on arrival. He believes repeated instances of non-compliance are indicative of a programming error.
MD88 Captain failed to set intersection crossing altitude restriction into the FMS and flight crew missed restriction by 6;000 FT.
MD-11 flight crew reported that an erroneous tire failure warning resulted in a precautionary landing.
Air carrier flight crew reported an altitude deviation during departure.
Pilot reported a runway incursion at JAC airport and cited snow obscuring the hold short line and the position of the Holding Position sign contributed to the event.
A C402 Captain detected smoke in the cockpit. He declared an emergency; notified ATC that he was securing his electrical system; and landed at the nearest suitable airport.
A corporate pilot taxied onto a runway because the taxiway marking near the ramp was not recognized as the hold short line and only after seeing the runway markings was the error recognized.
Air taxi pilot reported that smoke in the cockpit resulted in a diversion.

BE1900 Captain reports the landing gear relay circuit breaker tripping as the landing gear is selected down.  A go-around is initiated and the landing gear is extended manually.  A safe landing ensues; but the reporter states that landing gear malfunctions are a common occurrence at his company.
A320 Captain reported being issued taxi instructions to follow another aircraft and following the aircraft onto a runway to cross; but that was not ATC's intention.
Air carrier flight crew had an airborne conflict with a UAS while on final approach.
Flight Crew reported that the Flight Attendants reported an aft galley oven fire and were able to successfully extinguish the fire; allowing the flight to land safely at destination airport.
Air carrier Captain reported inadvertently entering into the FMS values that resulted in a crossing restriction not made.
EMB-145 Flight Attendant reported Captain notification of smoke in the passenger cabin during flight.

GA pilot reported inadvertently landing at F51 airport taxiway parallel to the runway of intended landing. The runway surface was rain-soaked and the markings were not clearly visible and in need of repainting; and the taxiway had a white centerline stripe; all of which contributed to the event.
Lear 75 Captain reported a loss of pressurization during climb that resulted in a return to the departure airport.
Flight crew reported incurring a runway incursion at PIT airport due to an unusual placement of hold short line; coupled with low visibility and snow.
Flight crew reported a runway incursion caused by lack of communication between crew members and not confirming the taxi route.
A PA28 instructor pilot reported that during climb they had a near miss with another PA28 that was on descent.
B-757 flight crew reported declaring an emergency and executing an uneventful emergency diversion due to smoke in the aft galley.
An Air Taxi crew taxied on the JAC Runway 19 overrun because the Commercial Airport Diagram did not depict an overrun and then faded markings gave the overrun the appearance of a Runway continuation.

A flight instructor and student pilot were advised by Air Traffic Control of another aircraft in their vicinity; but they were unable to acquire the traffic visually. While they were still climbing; and looking for the traffic; they were advised that the aircraft was descending through their altitude and within one mile. They pitched up aggressively and spotted traffic pass just beneath them.
After requesting and receiving a different runway for takeoff; crew was assigned a different departure procedure. Crew failed to notice the different final altitude clearance of the new departure.

Pilot reported landing gear failed to indicate extended and during alternate extension procedures; communications problems and failure to follow check lists resulted in the landing gear collapsing on landing roll out.
Air Carrier Captain reported a fume/smoke event in cockpit during departure taxi when windshield heat was activated.
B737 Captain reported an NMAC with another aircraft on approach to SAT that was not pointed out by ATC.
Pilot reported confusion when company aircraft taxiing behind them; transmitted clearance to cross runway in error.

Flight Attendant reports discovering smoke coming from an oven in the aft galley. The smoking oven is opened and sprayed with two Halon fire extinguishers while using a PBE. A great deal of smoke is generated and the flight diverts to the nearest suitable airport.
B737 flight crew reported missing a crossing restriction of 12;000 feet due to the restriction having been previously programed by the arrival as 12000A.
BOI Ground Controller reports of a near collision that happened with a passenger aircraft that had a runway incursion and an aircraft that was departing the airport.
An A319 flight crew reported deviating from cleared arrival into CLE when the FMS failed to load all the required waypoints.

A B767 First Officer on the Oceanic LAX SADDE Arrival was issued a constraint 60 west of VTU at FL190; but a previous FMC programming error correction deleted the restriction which caused them cross the restriction high.
I90 TRACON Controller reported on an air carrier Flight Crew report of a near miss with a UAV while on approach to IAH.
Air carrier flight crew had a near miss with a UAS while on a visual approach.
Corporate Captain reported an altitude deviation during climb and cited lack of flying as a contributing factor.
The pilot of a VANS RV reported that ATC alerted him to an immediate traffic conflict with another aircraft.

G280 First Officer described a track deviation when the Captain (pilot monitoring) attempted to program the FMC with a crossing restriction while talking to ATC. Somehow the FMC is sequenced to the next fix and the aircraft turns early. The Captain is unwilling to advise ATC of the FMC issues and request a vector.
An aircraft mistook an active runway for a taxiway and taxied onto the runway instead of crossing the runway.
B757-200 flight crew reported misinterpreted taxi instructions for another aircraft with a similar call sign; causing a runway incursion.
Flight crew reported crossing a runway; taxiing to parking; while not sure if the clearance instructions were for them due to Tower muffling the callsign.
Air Carrier First Officer reported an altitude deviation during approach caused by possible fatigue; a late runway change and lack of recent flying experience during the pandemic.

EMB145 First Officer reported entering the expected arrival and runway into the FMC prior to departure then not changing it when the airport switched from landing south to landing north. This resulted in a track deviation on the HYPER5 into IAD.
SA-227AC Captain reported the left main gear finally extended after multiple extension attempts.
